20:      * Expert waterfall over the assembled sections, contexts, tools, and variables.
21:      * Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): scoped listeners
22:      * receive only that scope's assemblies. The returned value is authoritative.
23:      * A supplied signal controls only this explicit assembly request and must not
24:      * be retained to control later turns. A registered complete section is

26:      * that scope's system prompt.
27:      * @param assembly - the mutable assembly built from registered providers.
28:      * @param context - the caller's per-assembly context.
29:      * @mode waterfall
30:      */
31:     'system-prompt/assemble'(this: Scoped<SystemPrompt>, assembly: PromptAssembly, context: AssembleContext, next: () => Promise<PromptAssembly>): Promise<PromptAssembly>
32:     /**
33:      * Emitted when any prompt provider changes. This registry notification is
34:      * unfiltered because a global change affects every scope.
35:      * @mode emit
36:      */

38:   }

44:    * Scope whose providers and waterfall listeners participate. When absent,
45:    * only global providers and subject-less listeners participate.
46:    */
47:   scope?: ScopeKey

49:   signal?: AbortSignal

52: /** One contributed section of the system prompt (registry input). */
53: export interface PromptSection {
54:   /** Unique name — a duplicate registration throws (see {@link SystemPrompt.section}). */
55:   readonly name: string
56:   /**
57:    * Sections are concatenated in ascending order. Equal orders use code-unit
58:    * name order.
59:    */

61:   /**
62:    * Static text or a provider evaluated at each assembly with that assembly's
63:    * {@link AssembleContext}. The text may reference `{{variable}}`s — they are
64:    * interpolated later, by {@link renderPrompt}, unless `interpolate` is false.
65:    */
66:   readonly text: string | ((context: AssembleContext) => string)
67:   /** Whether to interpolate prompt variables. Defaults to true; false preserves literal text. */
68:   readonly interpolate?: boolean
69:   /**
70:    * Treat this contribution as the complete system prompt. Assembly still
71:    * runs the cooperative waterfall so tools, contexts, and variables can be
72:    * resolved, then restores this exact section as the sole prompt section.
73:    * More than one effective complete section makes assembly fail.
74:    */

184: /**
185:  * The deployment persona prefix's section name. Exported because a
186:  * composition can replace this slot — an agent preset shadows the
187:  * deployment's persona with its own — and both sides naming the same section
188:  * is what makes the replacement work rather than duplicate.
189:  */
190: export const PERSONA_PREFIX_SECTION = 'deployment:persona-prefix'

192: /** Deployment persona suffix section name shared by global and scoped contributions. */
193: export const PERSONA_SUFFIX_SECTION = 'deployment:persona-suffix'

195: /** Valid variable names: how they are written between the braces. */
196: const VARIABLE_NAME = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/
197: 
198: /** A complete `{{...}}` reference group at the scan position (validated after). */
199: const GROUP_AT = /^\{\{([^{}]*)\}\}/
200: 
201: /** Reserved {@link Config.toolOrder} marker for unlisted tools. */
202: export const TOOL_ORDER_REST = '<unlisted-tools>'
203: 
204: /**
205:  * Validate duplicate names and the required {@link TOOL_ORDER_REST} marker.
206:  * Registered names are checked later because plugins have not loaded yet.
207:  */
208: function validateToolOrder(toolOrder: string[] | undefined): string[] | undefined {
209:   if (toolOrder === undefined) return undefined
210:   const seen = new Set<string>()
211:   for (const name of toolOrder) {
212:     if (seen.has(name)) throw new Error(`toolOrder lists "${name}" more than once`)
213:     seen.add(name)
214:   }
215:   if (!seen.has(TOOL_ORDER_REST)) {
216:     throw new Error(`toolOrder must contain the "${TOOL_ORDER_REST}" rest entry (where unlisted tools are inserted)`)
217:   }
218:   return toolOrder
219: }
220: 
221: /**
222:  * Apply configured tool order, inserting unlisted tools lexicographically at
223:  * {@link TOOL_ORDER_REST}. Unknown configured names fail; known but restricted
224:  * names may be absent.
225:  */
226: function orderTools(tools: ToolSchema[], toolOrder: string[] | undefined, knownNames: ReadonlySet<string>): ToolSchema[] {
227:   const reserved = tools.find(tool => tool.name === TOOL_ORDER_REST)
228:   if (reserved !== undefined) {
229:     throw new Error(`tool provider returned reserved tool name "${TOOL_ORDER_REST}" (reserved for toolOrder's rest entry)`)
230:   }
231:   if (toolOrder === undefined) return tools.sort(compareToolNames)
232:   const unknown = toolOrder.filter(name => name !== TOOL_ORDER_REST && !knownNames.has(name))
233:   if (unknown.length > 0) {
234:     throw new Error(`toolOrder lists unregistered tool${unknown.length > 1 ? 's' : ''} ${unknown.map(name => `"${name}"`).join(', ')}; known tools: ${[...knownNames].sort().join(', ') || '(none)'}`)
235:   }
236:   const listed = new Set(toolOrder)
237:   const rest = tools.filter(tool => !listed.has(tool.name)).sort(compareToolNames)
238:   return toolOrder.flatMap(name =>
239:     name === TOOL_ORDER_REST ? rest : tools.filter(tool => tool.name === name))
240: }

242: /** Code-unit name comparison — locale-independent, so the order is identical on every machine. */
243: function compareNames(a: string, b: string): number {
244:   return a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0
245: }
246: 
247: /** Order prompt sections by their explicit placement, then deterministically by name. */
248: function comparePromptSections(a: PromptSection, b: PromptSection): number {
249:   return a.order - b.order || compareNames(a.name, b.name)
250: }
251: 
252: /** Order tool schemas lexicographically by name. */
253: function compareToolNames(a: ToolSchema, b: ToolSchema): number {
254:   return compareNames(a.name, b.name)
255: }

259:   /** Include the fixed DeepSeek Harness identity before the deployment persona (default true). */
260:   includeHarnessIdentity?: boolean
261:   /** Include optional runtime-context snapshots in model history (default true); required context remains. */
262:   includeRuntimeContext?: boolean
263:   /**
264:    * Deployment-wide persona prefix template before first-party guidance. A scoped section named
265:    * `deployment:persona-prefix` shadows it; `{{variable}}` references are strict.

267:   personaPrefix?: string
268:   /**
269:    * Persona suffix template after first-party guidance. A scoped `deployment:persona-suffix`
270:    * section shadows it; `{{variable}}` references are strict. Defaults to empty.
271:    */
272:   personaSuffix?: string
273:   /**
274:    * Model-facing tool names in order, with {@link TOOL_ORDER_REST} exactly once.
275:    * Invalid fields fail at load and unknown names fail at assembly; known names
276:    * hidden in one scope may be absent there. Omitted means lexicographic order.
277:    */
278:   toolOrder?: string[]
279: }

281: /**
282:  * Interpolate strict `{{variable}}` references, drop empty sections, and join
283:  * the rest with blank lines. Sections with `interpolate: false` retain literal
284:  * text. Malformed, unknown, or undefined references in other sections throw;
285:  * a lone `{{` without any later `}}` is literal prose, and substituted values
286:  * are not scanned again.
287:  * @param assembly - the assembly whose sections and variables to render.
288:  * @returns the rendered prompt, or `''` when all sections are empty.
289:  */
290: export function renderPrompt(assembly: PromptAssembly): string {
291:   return assembly.sections
292:     .map(section => section.interpolate === false ? section.text : interpolate(section, assembly.variables, 'section'))
293:     .filter(text => text.length > 0)
294:     .join('\n\n')
295: }
296: 
297: /**
298:  * Render the complete dynamic context snapshot, preserving literal contributions.
299:  * @param assembly - the assembly whose contexts and variables to render.
300:  * @returns the current full snapshot, or `''` when no context is active.
301:  */
302: export function renderContextSnapshot(assembly: PromptAssembly): string {
303:   return joinContextSections(renderContextSections(assembly))
304: }
305: 
306: /**
307:  * The model-facing snapshot text for an already-rendered section list.
308:  *
309:  * A caller that also needs the sections renders them once and joins here, so a
310:  * request does not interpolate every context twice.
311:  * @param sections - sections from {@link renderContextSections}.
312:  * @returns the current full snapshot, or `''` when no context is active.
313:  */
314: export function joinContextSections(sections: readonly ContextSnapshotSection[]): string {
315:   const body = sections.map(section => section.text).join('\n\n')
316:   if (body.length === 0) return ''
317:   return `Current runtime context. This snapshot supersedes earlier runtime-context snapshots.\n\n${body}`
318: }
319: 
320: /**
321:  * The same snapshot, kept as the named contributions it was assembled from.
322:  *
323:  * {@link renderContextSnapshot} joins these for the model; a consumer that
324:  * presents the snapshot uses them to attribute each part to the subsystem that
325:  * contributed it, without re-splitting the joined prose. Contributions with
326:  * `interpolate: false` preserve literal text instead of resolving prompt variables.
327:  * @param assembly - the assembly whose contexts and variables to render.
328:  * @returns one entry per contributing context that rendered to non-empty text.
329:  */
330: export function renderContextSections(assembly: PromptAssembly): ContextSnapshotSection[] {
331:   return assembly.contexts
332:     .map(context => ({
333:       name: context.name,
334:       text: context.interpolate === false ? context.text : interpolate(context, assembly.variables, 'context'),
335:     }))
336:     .filter(section => section.text.length > 0)
337: }

339: /** Interpolate one section or context and attribute diagnostics to its owning input. */
340: function interpolate(
341:   input: AssembledSection | AssembledContext,
342:   variables: Record<string, string | undefined>,
343:   kind: 'section' | 'context',
344: ): string {
345:   const text = input.text
346:   let result = ''
347:   let last = 0
348:   for (let open = text.indexOf('{{'); open >= 0; open = text.indexOf('{{', last)) {
349:     const group = GROUP_AT.exec(text.slice(open))
350:     if (group === null) {
351:       // A later closing brace makes this malformed; otherwise it is literal prose.
352:       if (text.indexOf('}}', open + 2) >= 0) {
353:         throw new Error(`malformed prompt variable reference at "${text.slice(open, open + 16)}…" in ${kind} "${input.name}" (references are complete simple {{name}} groups)`)
354:       }
355:       result += text.slice(last, open + 2)
356:       last = open + 2
357:       continue
358:     }
359:     // `{{}}` yields an empty name and follows the malformed-reference path.
360:     const name = group[0].slice(2, -2)
361:     if (!VARIABLE_NAME.test(name)) {
362:       throw new Error(`malformed prompt variable reference "{{${name}}}" in ${kind} "${input.name}" (variable names match ${String(VARIABLE_NAME)})`)
363:     }
364:     // Do not resolve unregistered names through Object.prototype.
365:     if (!Object.hasOwn(variables, name)) {
366:       const known = Object.keys(variables)
367:       throw new Error(`unknown prompt variable "{{${name}}}" in ${kind} "${input.name}"; registered variables: ${known.length > 0 ? known.join(', ') : '(none)'}`)
368:     }
369:     const value = variables[name]
370:     if (value === undefined) {
371:       throw new Error(`prompt variable "{{${name}}}" has no value for this assembly (${kind} "${input.name}")`)
372:     }
373:     result += text.slice(last, open) + value
374:     last = open + group[0].length
375:   }
376:   return result + text.slice(last)
377: }

379: /** Resolve one registered runtime fact without assembling sections or tools. */
380: function resolveContext(entry: PromptContext, context: AssembleContext): AssembledContext {
381:   return {
382:     name: entry.name,
383:     text: typeof entry.text === 'function' ? entry.text(context) : entry.text,
384:     ...entry.interpolate !== undefined ? { interpolate: entry.interpolate } : {},
385:   }
386: }

394: /** All prompt registrations owned by one global or scoped layer. */
395: class PromptLayer implements ScopeLayer {
396:   readonly sections: NamedEntries<PromptSection>
397:   readonly contexts: NamedEntries<PromptContext>
398:   readonly runtimeContextSuppressors = new AnonymousEntries<true>()
399:   readonly toolProviders = new AnonymousEntries<ToolProvider>()
400:   readonly variables: NamedEntries<VariableProvider>
401: 
402:   /**
403:    * Create one prompt layer with diagnostics specific to its ownership scope.
404:    * @param scope - the scoped owner, or `undefined` for global registrations.
405:    */
406:   constructor(scope: ScopeKey | undefined) {
407:     this.sections = new NamedEntries(name => new Error(scope === undefined
408:       ? `prompt section "${name}" is already registered (for a per-agent override, register through that agent's \`agent.ctx\` instead)`
409:       : `prompt section "${name}" is already registered in this scope`))
410:     this.contexts = new NamedEntries(name => new Error(scope === undefined
411:       ? `prompt context "${name}" is already registered (for a per-agent override, register through that agent's \`agent.ctx\` instead)`
412:       : `prompt context "${name}" is already registered in this scope`))
413:     this.variables = new NamedEntries(name => new Error(scope === undefined
414:       ? `prompt variable "${name}" is already registered (for a per-agent value, register through that agent's \`agent.ctx\` instead)`
415:       : `prompt variable "${name}" is already registered in this scope`))
416:   }
417: 
418:   /** @returns whether this layer owns no prompt registrations. */
419:   isEmpty(): boolean {
420:     return this.sections.isEmpty()
421:       && this.contexts.isEmpty()
422:       && this.runtimeContextSuppressors.isEmpty()
423:       && this.toolProviders.isEmpty()
424:       && this.variables.isEmpty()
425:   }
426: }

428: /** Registry service for the prompt inputs assembled before each model step. */
429: export class SystemPrompt extends Service {
430:   static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
431:     includeHarnessIdentity: z.boolean().default(true),
432:     includeRuntimeContext: z.boolean().default(true),
433:     personaPrefix: z.string().default(''),
434:     personaSuffix: z.string().default(''),
435:     // Preserve omission because an explicit empty order lacks the rest marker.
436:     toolOrder: z.array(z.string()).default(undefined as unknown as string[]),
437:   })
438: 
439:   private readonly layers = new ScopedLayers(
440:     scope => new PromptLayer(scope),
441:     () => { this.ctx.emit('system-prompt/change') },
442:   )
443:   private readonly toolOrder: string[] | undefined
444: 
445:   constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
446:     super(ctx, 'systemPrompt')
447:     this.toolOrder = validateToolOrder(config.toolOrder)
448:     // Keep harness-owned openers independent of the selected loop plugin.
449:     if (config.includeHarnessIdentity ?? true) {
450:       this.section({
451:         name: 'harness:identity',
452:         order: this.getSectionOrder('HARNESS_IDENTITY'),
453:         text: 'You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.',
454:       })
455:     }
456:     this.section({

458:       order: this.getSectionOrder('DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_PREFIX'),
459:       // The fallback narrows the optional input type; the schema already defaults it.
460:       text: config.personaPrefix ?? '',

463:       name: PERSONA_SUFFIX_SECTION,
464:       order: this.getSectionOrder('DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_SUFFIX'),
465:       text: config.personaSuffix ?? '',
466:     })

468:   }
469: 
470:   /**
471:    * Register an ordered prompt section in the calling context's scope. A scoped
472:    * section shadows a global section with the same name; duplicates within one
473:    * layer and non-finite orders throw. Registration and disposal emit
474:    * `system-prompt/change`.
475:    * @param section - the section to register.
476:    * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer.
477:    */
478:   section(section: PromptSection): () => void {
479:     if (!Number.isFinite(section.order)) {
480:       throw new TypeError(`prompt section "${section.name}" order must be a finite number`)
481:     }
482:     return this.layers.effect(
483:       this.ctx,
484:       layer => layer.sections.insert(section.name, section),
485:       { label: 'systemPrompt.section()' },
486:     )
487:   }
488: 
489:   /**
490:    * Resolve the centrally owned placement of a repository prompt section.
491:    * @param name - stable section placement name.
492:    * @returns the section's numeric sort order.
493:    */
494:   getSectionOrder(name: PromptSectionOrderName): number {
495:     return SECTION_ORDERS[name]
496:   }
497: 
498:   /**
499:    * Resolve the centrally owned placement of a repository runtime context.
500:    * @param name - stable context placement name.
501:    * @returns the context's numeric sort order.
502:    */
503:   getContextOrder(name: PromptContextOrderName): number {
504:     return CONTEXT_ORDERS[name]
505:   }
506: 
507:   /**
508:    * Register ordered dynamic context in the calling context's scope. Scoped
509:    * entries shadow global entries with the same name.
510:    * @param context - the context contribution to register.
511:    * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer.
512:    */
513:   context(context: PromptContext): () => void {
514:     if (!Number.isFinite(context.order)) {
515:       throw new TypeError(`prompt context "${context.name}" order must be a finite number`)
516:     }
517:     return this.layers.effect(
518:       this.ctx,
519:       layer => layer.contexts.insert(context.name, context),
520:       { label: 'systemPrompt.context()' },
521:     )
522:   }
523: 
524:   /**
525:    * Suppress optional dynamic runtime-context contributions in the calling
526:    * context's scope without changing the services that own or enforce those
527:    * facts. Multiple suppressors remain independently disposable.
528:    * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer.
529:    */
530:   suppressRuntimeContext(): () => void {
531:     return this.layers.effect(
532:       this.ctx,
533:       layer => layer.runtimeContextSuppressors.append(true),
534:       { label: 'systemPrompt.suppressRuntimeContext()' },
535:     )
536:   }
537: 
538:   /**
539:    * Register a tool-schema provider in the calling context's scope. Global and
540:    * matching scoped providers both contribute; returning the reserved
541:    * {@link TOOL_ORDER_REST} name makes assembly fail.
542:    * @param provider - evaluated for each assembly with its context.
543:    * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer.
544:    */
545:   tools(provider: (context: AssembleContext) => ToolProviderResult): () => void {
546:     return this.layers.effect(
547:       this.ctx,
548:       layer => layer.toolProviders.append(provider),
549:       { label: 'systemPrompt.tools()' },
550:     )
551:   }
552: 
553:   /**
554:    * Register a prompt variable in the calling context's scope. Scoped values
555:    * shadow globals; invalid or duplicate names throw. A provider may return
556:    * `undefined`, but rendering a section that references that value then fails.
557:    * @param name - the `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` reference name.
558:    * @param provider - evaluated for each assembly.
559:    * @returns the exact Cordis effect disposer.
560:    */
561:   variable(name: string, provider: (context: AssembleContext) => string | undefined): () => void {
562:     if (!VARIABLE_NAME.test(name)) {
563:       throw new Error(`invalid prompt variable name "${name}" (must match ${String(VARIABLE_NAME)})`)
564:     }
565:     return this.layers.effect(
566:       this.ctx,
567:       layer => layer.variables.insert(name, provider),
568:       { label: 'systemPrompt.variable()' },
569:     )
570:   }
571: 
572:   /**
573:    * Refresh accepted registered runtime facts for request admission. Contexts
574:    * added only by the assembly waterfall retain their accepted values. Current
575:    * suppression removes optional contexts, and missing required registrations
576:    * are restored in registry order. Sections, tools, and interpolation variables
577:    * retain the accepted assembly; their providers and waterfall do not rerun.
578:    * @param assembly - accepted assembly for this scope and step.
579:    * @param context - the same scope and current plugin-defined assembly fields.
580:    * @returns the accepted assembly with current runtime-context provider text.
581:    */
582:   refreshContext(assembly: PromptAssembly, context: AssembleContext = {}): PromptAssembly {
583:     const providers = this.layers.merge(context.scope, layer => layer.contexts)
584:     const suppressed = !this.layers.global.runtimeContextSuppressors.isEmpty()
585:       || this.layers.chainLayers(context.scope).some(layer => !layer.runtimeContextSuppressors.isEmpty())
586:     const required = new Map([...providers].filter(([, entry]) => entry.required === true))
587:     const contexts: AssembledContext[] = []
588:     for (const accepted of assembly.contexts) {
589:       const provider = providers.get(accepted.name)
590:       required.delete(accepted.name)
591:       if (suppressed && provider?.required !== true) continue
592:       contexts.push(provider === undefined ? accepted : resolveContext(provider, context))
593:     }
594:     for (const provider of required.values()) {
595:       const index = contexts.findIndex((entry) => {
596:         const next = providers.get(entry.name)
597:         return next !== undefined && next.order > provider.order
598:       })
599:       contexts.splice(index < 0 ? contexts.length : index, 0, resolveContext(provider, context))
600:     }
601:     return { ...assembly, contexts }
602:   }
603: 
604:   /**
605:    * Assemble global and scoped providers, detach tool parameters, apply
606:    * canonical ordering, then run the assembly waterfall. Scoped sections and
607:    * variables shadow globals. The returned waterfall value is authoritative
608:    * except that an effective complete section is restored afterwards as the
609:    * sole prompt section.
610:    * @param context - the optional scope and plugin-defined assembly fields.
611:    * @returns the post-waterfall assembly with any complete prompt enforced.
612:    */
613:   // Keep configuration failures on the declared asynchronous error path.
614:   async assemble(context: AssembleContext = {}): Promise<PromptAssembly> {
615:     const scope = context.scope
616:     const scopeLayers = this.layers.chainLayers(scope)
617:     const runtimeContextSuppressed = !this.layers.global.runtimeContextSuppressors.isEmpty()
618:       || scopeLayers.some(layer => !layer.runtimeContextSuppressors.isEmpty())
619:     // Scoped variables shadow globals.
620:     const variables: Record<string, string | undefined> = {}
621:     for (const [name, provider] of this.layers.global.variables.entries()) {
622:       variables[name] = provider(context)
623:     }
624:     // Scope-chain variables, farthest first, so the nearest scope wins a name.
625:     for (const layer of scopeLayers) {
626:       for (const [name, provider] of layer.variables.entries()) {
627:         variables[name] = provider(context)
628:       }
629:     }
630:     // Scoped sections shadow globals before the deterministic order sort.
631:     const sectionByName = this.layers.merge(scope, layer => layer.sections)
632:     const contextByName = this.layers.merge(scope, layer => layer.contexts)
633:     // Validate order against pre-restriction names while collecting visible schemas.
634:     const providers = [
635:       ...this.layers.global.toolProviders.values(),
636:       ...scopeLayers.flatMap(layer => [...layer.toolProviders.values()]),
637:     ]
638:     const collected: ToolSchema[] = []
639:     const knownNames = new Set<string>()
640:     for (const provider of providers) {
641:       const result = provider(context)
642:       const schemas = result.schemas.map(({ name, description, parameters, deferLoading }): ToolSchema => ({
643:         name,
644:         description,
645:         parameters: structuredClone(parameters),
646:         ...deferLoading === true ? { deferLoading } : {},
647:       }))
648:       const acceptedKnownNames = result.knownNames ?? schemas.map(tool => tool.name)
649:       collected.push(...schemas)
650:       for (const name of acceptedKnownNames) knownNames.add(name)
651:     }
652:     const sectionDefinitions = [...sectionByName.values()].sort(comparePromptSections)
653:     const completeSections = sectionDefinitions.filter(section => section.complete === true)
654:     if (completeSections.length > 1) {
655:       throw new Error(`multiple complete prompt sections are active: ${completeSections.map(section => JSON.stringify(section.name)).join(', ')}`)
656:     }
657:     let completeSection: AssembledSection | undefined
658:     const sections = sectionDefinitions
659:       .map((section) => {
660:         const assembled = {
661:           name: section.name,
662:           text: typeof section.text === 'function' ? section.text(context) : section.text,
663:           ...section.interpolate !== undefined ? { interpolate: section.interpolate } : {},
664:         }
665:         if (section.complete === true) completeSection = { ...assembled }
666:         return assembled
667:       })
668:     const assembly: PromptAssembly = {
669:       sections,
670:       contexts: [...contextByName.values()]

672:         .sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order)
673:         .map(entry => resolveContext(entry, context)),
674:       tools: orderTools(collected, this.toolOrder, knownNames),
675:       variables,
676:     }
677:     const transformed = await this.ctx.waterfall(
678:       scopeTarget(this, scope), 'system-prompt/assemble', assembly, context,
679:       () => Promise.resolve(assembly),
680:     )
681:     if (completeSection === undefined && !runtimeContextSuppressed) return transformed
682:     const requiredContexts = new Set([...contextByName.values()].filter(entry => entry.required === true).map(entry => entry.name))
683:     return {
684:       ...transformed,
685:       sections: completeSection === undefined ? transformed.sections : [completeSection],
686:       contexts: runtimeContextSuppressed ? transformed.contexts.filter(entry => requiredContexts.has(entry.name)) : transformed.contexts,

Explain in three short bullets how system prompt sections are ordered and joined.

Key points:
1. Ordering: sections sorted by ascending numeric `order` (from SECTION_ORDERS central table), ties broken by code-unit name comparison (comparePromptSections).
2. Joining/rendering: renderPrompt maps each section, interpolating `{{variables}}` unless `interpolate: false`, drops empty sections, joins remaining with '\n\n' (blank line).
3. Special cases: scoped sections shadow global ones with the same name before sorting; a `complete` section replaces the whole prompt as the sole section after the waterfall. Also runtime contexts are separate (joined with '\n\n' and prefixed by snapshot banner).

Three short bullets.

- **Order:** Every section carries a numeric `order` — usually pulled from the central `SECTION_ORDERS` table (`HARNESS_IDENTITY: -1000` … `HARNESS_SOURCE: 10000`). Assembly sorts ascending by `order`, with ties broken by code-unit name comparison (`comparePromptSections`, [index.ts:248](packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts#L248)), so the result is deterministic across machines.
- **Join:** `renderPrompt` maps each section (interpolating `{{variables}}` unless `interpolate: false`), drops any that render to empty text, and concatenates the rest with a blank line (`'\n\n'`) — [index.ts:290](packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts#L290).
- **Overrides:** Before sorting, scoped sections shadow global sections of the same name; and if any section is marked `complete`, that exact section is restored after the assembly waterfall as the *sole* prompt section, so nothing else is joined around it.
